Logan,

Thanks for taking the RFP. We're in the final 2 weeks of vendor responses and have a focused set of technical questions around encryption and key custody to validate for procurement. I attached the worksheet with specific rows that need short answers. Top-line ask: can Redwood support BYOK import into a customer-controlled HSM (PKCS#11-compatible), and can you provide evidence (attestation or HSM config screenshots) that import is performed with customer-wrapped keys only?

Other items in the sheet: key rotation windows, supported wrapping algorithms, TLS cipher suites for inter-service communication, and audit log retention for key operations.

Can you reply with short answers and any artifacts you can share? Timing: ideally by end of week so we can include in evaluator packet.

Jordan — thanks for the worksheet. We reviewed and provided concise responses inline in the attached spreadsheet (see tab "Redwood answers"). High level summary here so your team can triage quickly:

- BYOK import: Supported in Redwood Private and Dedicated via customer-supplied wrapping key. Imports are performed via RSA-OAEP or ECDH-based wrapping; Redwood never has access to private material in the clear. For on-prem deployments we can also deploy an HSM appliance in-customer-network.
- HSM compatibility: Our import/export layer is compatible with PKCS#11 v2.40 endpoints; we support AWS CloudHSM and common FIPS-validated appliances.
- Attestation/evidence: We can provide a FIPS attestation PDF, import logs (redacted), and an import transcript showing the public-wrapped key fingerprint. I attached the FIPS doc and a BYO diagram for clarity.
- Rotation: Primary policy is customer-controlled rotation schedule. Default recommended rotation is 90 days for wrapping keys and 365 days for data-encryption keys; we support programmatic rotation via API and can do emergency (ad-hoc) rotations with immediate key rewrap.
- TLS: Inter-service TLS uses TLS1.3 (preferred) and TLS1.2 with strong cipher suites; mutual TLS is supported for customer-facing endpoints.
- Audit logs: Key usage and import/export operations are logged with 13 months retention in the default tenant; retention can be extended for Dedicated/Private customers.

Next steps: we propose a short technical validation session (30–45 minutes) with your security engineering team to run a canary import and verify the import transcript. Suggested times attached in the Drive link.

If that works, I'll coordinate with Mina and Karthik for the demo and to pull the attestation artifacts.

Cheers,
Logan Wright

Jordan — adding a few technical clarifications to Logan's summary (quoting his reply below for context).

On BYOK import and HSM specifics:
- Import flow: customer generates an asymmetric wrapping keypair (recommended RSA 4096 or X25519/ECDH). Customer supplies the public wrapping key to Redwood over an authenticated channel (S/MIME, signed email, or the provisioning API over mTLS). Redwood wraps the key material using the provided public key; only the wrapped blob is stored in transit.
- Supported wrapping algorithms: RSA-OAEP-SHA256 and ECDH-ES with AES-KW are both supported for imports. We keep an import transcript with the public key fingerprint, import timestamp, and the PKCS#11 slot identifier (for on-prem HSMs).
- PKCS#11 & HSMs: Our connector speaks PKCS#11 v2.40 and can operate against CloudHSM clusters, Thales Luna, and vendor appliances that expose a PKCS#11 interface. For Dedicated customers we can configure a direct HSM binding; for Private (VPC) we ship a connector that runs in the customer's tenant.
- Attestation: The FIPS attestation we shared covers our HSM module and build pipeline as of 2026-07. For customers requiring stronger evidence, Redwood can coordinate a joint inspection with the HSM vendor for an export-proof demo.
- Key rotation and lifecycle: We recommend tenant-level policies. Typical defaults we offer: wrapping key rotation every 90 days, DEK (data encryption key) rotation every 365 days, with support for on-demand rotation. Rotations are non-blocking: data keys are re-encrypted (envelope rewrap) in the background, and there is a configurable grace period (default 7 days) where both old and new keys are accepted for reads.
- Emergency rotation: we support immediate rewrap with audit-recorded forced-rollovers; rollback is controlled and requires two internal approvers for Dedicated/Private.

Logs & evidence: all key operations generate entries in our audit stream (operation type, initiator ID, request/response hashes). We can export a signed digest of a selected time range as a tarball for audit.

Thanks Logan and Mina — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our procurement and security teams after reviewing the spreadsheet and attestation:

1) Key escrow/escrow prohibition: We need confirmation in writing that Redwood will not retain unwrapped private keys or escrow material and that exported artifacts are limited to wrapped blobs and logs. Is that acceptable?

2) Tenant wrapping vs vendor-wrapping: For our architecture we prefer tenant-side wrapping where our KMS holds the master wrapping key. Can you confirm whether Redwood can operate in a mode where only the customer-held wrapping key ever has the ability to unwrap? (Specifically: no Redwood operator or service account can unwrap).

3) On-prem HSM option: For regulated workloads we may require the HSM physically in our datacenter (or as an HSM appliance in our VPC). Can you outline the differences in attestation and operational model between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private with respect to HSM custody and where the private wrapping key resides?

4) Validation timeline: we need to schedule that canary import/demo early next week — what windows do you have? Also procurement needs the signed attestation as a PDF with a Redwood exec signature on file.

Appreciate the quick turn.

—Elena Soto
Security Architecture, AcmeHealth

Elena — thanks for the clarifying questions. Short answers inline, then next steps.

1) Key escrow: Redwood will not retain unwrapped customer private keys. Imports are stored only as wrapped blobs; private key material is never persisted in cleartext by Redwood. We will include a short contract clause (non-escrow) in the SOW and can add language to the MSA if needed.

2) Tenant-side wrapping mode: Yes — supported. In tenant-side wrapping the customer-supplied wrapping key is the only key that can unwrap imported DEKs; Redwood operators do not have access to unwrap. For Hosted customers this is enabled via our mTLS provisioning API + customer public key; for Dedicated/Private the same model applies with connector-level PKCS#11 bindings. We'll include a configuration checklist for your engineers.

3) On-prem HSM differences:
- Hosted: Redwood hosts HSM-backed services; we can accept customer-wrapped key imports and provide import transcripts. Attestation comes from our FIPS artifact and signed logs.
- Dedicated: HSM(s) are dedicated to a customer in our region/zone — admin plane access is gated by the customer's admin roles.
- Private (VPC/appliance): HSM physically resides in the customer's environment; Redwood's control plane manages metadata only. In Private, the customer's HSM vendor provides the attestation; Redwood facilitates the joint validation and can produce signed operation digests.

4) Timeline & artifacts: We can run the canary import during the week of Nov 9. Proposed slots: Mon 11/9 10:00–11:00 PT or Tue 11/10 14:00–15:00 PT. Please confirm which works and we'll provision a short test environment. I'll also ask our legal team to produce the attestation cover letter with an exec signature and provide it ahead of the demo.

Next steps (short):
- Confirm demo slot (pick one)
- Jordan/Elena to provide public wrapping key and a sample import key ID (or we can generate a test pair)
- We'll run the canary import, capture the transcript, and provide signed logs + the attestation PDF before procurement cut-off.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.
